Refers to Gran Buenos Aires. Data for 2001 and 2010 refer to the urban agglomeration including Buenos Aires city, 24 districts of Gran Buenos Aires and some districts of the suburbs.
Refers to Significant Urban Areas as of 2001.

The data include communities under the authority of the Town Council. The 1989 census produced data referring to the city proper only; the population of the urban agglomeration for that date was estimated by assuming that the ratio of the population of the urban agglomeration to that of the city proper was the same as in 1979.

Refers to the municipality of Phnon Penh including suburban areas.
Refers to the Census Metropolitan Area. The capital is Ottawa.
Data from 1952 to 1992 refer to Gran Santiago. Data for 2002 and 2012 refer to the urban population of Santiago Metropolitan Area Region.

For the 1982 and 1990 censuses, the data reflect all residents of urban areas of the city (excluding Yanqing District). For the 2000 and 2010 censuses, the population of the city is composed of population in all city districts (excluding Yanqing District) meeting the criteria such as contiguous built-up areas, being the location of the local government, being a Street or Having a Resident Committee.
Data refer to the urban population of the Distrito Especial de Bogotá, and the capitals of the municipalities of Chia, Funza and Soacha (cabeceras municipales).
Refers to the urban population of the cantons.
Refers to the settlement of Zagreb.
Refers to the Greater Copenhagen Region as defined from 1999 onward consisting of (parts of) 16 municipalities. The limits of the urban agglomeration have been modified between 1970 and 1976.
Data refer to the population of the “cercle”.
Data for 2002 and 2010 refer to the urban population of the Municipalities of Santo Domingo de Guzmán, Santo Domingo Este, Santo Domingo Oeste, and Santo Domingo Norte, as of 2010.

Data from 1960 to 1986 refer to the Governorate of Al-Qahirah (Cairo) and the cities of Al-Jizah (Giza) and Shubra al-Khaymah (Shubra-El-Khema). Data for 1996 and 2006 refer to Greater Cairo as the sum of the Governorate of Al-Qahirah (Cairo) and the surrounding districts of the Governorates of Al-Jizah (Giza) and Al-Qalyübyah (Qalyubia).
Refers to the urban population of the municipios of San Salvador, Mejicanos, Soyapango, Delgado, Ilopango, Cuscatancingo, Ayutuxtepeque, and San Marcos.
Mbabane is the administrative capital and Lobamba is the legislative capital.
Refers to the local government areas of Banjul and Kanifing.
Data refer to the localities of Calithèa, Peristérion and Piraeus, among others.
Refers to St. George Parish.

Data for 1971 and later refer to urban agglomeration. Data for 1950 refer to city proper. 1999 estimate refers to the urban agglomeration of Port-au-Prince, Delmas and Carrefour. As of 1 February 2010, the impact of the earthquake on 12 January 2010 is estimated with the data from the Government of Haiti and the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

Data for 1991, 2001 and 2011 refer to the metropolitan area that is not restricted to state boundaries (National Capital Territory). Contiguous suburban cities and towns, such as Faridabad, Gurgaon, and Ghaziabad are included in Dehli. The capital is New Delhi. The official estimates for New Delhi and Delhi Urban Agglomeration were 257,803 and 16,349,831 in the year 2011, respectively.

Data refer to the functional urban area, that is, contiguous areas which are consistently urban in character as indicated by levels of population density, economic functions and facilities. Jakarta covers five municipalities (kotamadya): Jakarta Selatan, Jakarta Timur, Jakarta Pusat, Jakarta Barat, and Jakarta Utara. Data for 1990 does not refer to the functional urban area. Appropriate estimates were derived by using the ratio of the population in the functional urban area to that of the population in the relevant municipalities as derived from the 1980 census.

Designation and data provided by Israel. The position of the United Nations on the question of Jerusalem is contained in General Assembly resolution 181 (II) and subsequent resolutions of the General Assembly and the Security Council concerning this question. Including data for East Jerusalem.
Since 1991, the official Metropolitan City.

Major Metropolitan areas (M.M.A.) are defined by the Statistics Bureau of Japan. Census figures for 2005, 2010 and 2015 refer to the Kanto M.M.A.; figures from 1990 to 2000 are based on the Keihinyo M.M.A., and figures from 1960 to 1985 are based on the Keihin M.M.A. As a reference, the population of Tokyo-to was estimated at 12.1 million persons and of the Tokyo Ku-area at 8.1 million in 2000.
Refers to the island of Tarawa. The capital is Bairiki, located on that island. The population of Bairiki was estimated at 3,218 in the year 2015.

Data for 2005 and 2011 refer to the Governorates of Capital, Hawalli, Al-Farwaniya and Mubarak Al-Kabeer. Data for 1985 and 1995 refer to the Governorates of Capital, Hawalli and Al-Farwaniya. The number and names of governorates have changed over time as well as the limits of the urban agglomeration.
There is some level of uncertainty with respect to the estimates for Bayrut. Excluding Syrian Refugees.
Refers to the Greater Kuala Lumpur. Kuuala Lumpur is the capital and Putrajaya is the administrative capital.
Refers to the localities of the Northern Harbour and Southern Harbour.
Refers to the total population in seventy-six municipalities of the Metropolitan Area of Mexico City.
Refers to the urban population of Podgorica municipality.
Includes Salé and Temara.

Refers to the municipalities of s-Gravenhage, Leidschendam, Leidschendam-Voorburg, Rijswijk, Voorburg, Wassenaar, Wateringen.
The limits of the urban agglomeration have been modified between 2001 and 2006.
Data for 1953 and 1963 refer to city proper. Data for 1991, 2006 and 2013 refer to urban agglomeration.

Refers to Muscat governorate, which consists of the Wilayas of Muscat, Mutrah, Bawshar, As Seeb, and Al Amrat (excluding Wilaya of Qurayyat).  For the year 2016, refers to the sum of Muscat, Mutrah, Bawshar and As Seeb.

Refers to the metropolitan area of Panama City, made up of the population of urban localities in the districts of Panamá, Arraijan, La Chorrera and San Miguelito. Data for 1980 includes the urban population in the district of Balboa.
Refers to the district of Asunción and the 19 districts of Central Department.
Refers to the Province of Lima and the Constitutional Province of Callao.
Refers to the National Capital Region.
Refers to Grande Lisboa, the Peninsula of Setúbal, and the municipality Azambuja.

Refers to the sum of the Departments of Dakar, Pikinie and Guédiawaye, in Dakar Region.
Refers to the urban population of Belgrade area.
Refers to the urban agglomeration of 1972.
The 2012 census enumeration was done on the de jure basis, while the 2001 census enumeration was done on de facto basis.
Refers to the total population of District of Paramaribo.

Considering the situation in the country, recent estimates should be used with caution as they are not based on solid evidence.

Refers to Grand Tunis, which consists of the communal (urban) populations in the Governorates of Tunis, Ariana and Ben Arous.
Refers to Altindag, Cankaya, Etimesgut, Golbasi, Keçioren, Mamak, Sincan and Yenimahalle.
Data for 2014 also includes Kira, Makindye Ssabagabo and Nansana. The population of Kampala (city proper) was reported as 1,507,080 in 2014.
Data for 1951, 1961 and 1971 refer to "Conurbation". Data from 1981 onwards refer to "Urban area" (Greater London).

Data from 1963 to 1985 refer to the department of Montevideo and localities of the department of Canelones. Data from 1996 to 2011 refer to the department of Montevideo and localities of the departments of Canelones and San José (Cerámicas del Sur and Ciudad del Plata).

Refers to the Municipality of El Libertador in the Federal District, the Municipality of Sucre in the State of Miranda, and the parishes of Carrizal (Municipality of Carrizal), Cecilio Acosta (Municipality of Guaicaipuro), and San Antonio (Municipality of Las Salias) in the State of Miranda.
Data refer to urban population in the city districts. Data after 2008 include urban population in former Ha Tay Province.
Data for 1950,1960 and 1975 refer to city proper. Data for 1986,1994 ,2004 and 2009 refer to urban agglomeration.
